passages.title: A seed collection with missing stories

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: At a fictional regional garden, staff discovered a box of seeds collected during a survey forty years earlier. Labels gave dates and locations, but rarely described how many plants had been sampled. The collection was potentially useful for studying change, yet it could not be assumed to represent the full diversity of the original populations. A single productive plant might have supplied most seeds in an envelope.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Before attempting large-scale germination, the curator set aside a small sample from each envelope for a pilot test. The aim was to learn which storage histories were associated with survival while preserving material for later work. Seeds that did not germinate were not automatically classified as dead: some species require a period of cold or other environmental signals before growth begins. The team tested several treatments and documented them individually.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Local residents supplied photographs and notebooks describing the survey. These sources clarified some collection routes, although memories sometimes disagreed with written dates. The curator retained both accounts with an explanation of the discrepancy instead of choosing whichever seemed more convenient. The project could reveal which surviving seeds responded to particular treatments. It could not reconstruct all the genetic variation that had existed in the landscape forty years earlier.
